SWMM5 Implicit Box Solver Test Bench

EPA SWMM 5.2.4 + pbox.c · modified engine · build 2026-10-02

Runs one .inp twice in your browser: once with stock SWMM 5.2.4 dynamic wave, once with an implicit Preissmann four-point box scheme built into the same engine. The implicit scheme is the published method InfoWorks ICM's 1D engine is documented as using. It is not InfoWorks code and will not reproduce InfoWorks numbers.

1. Choose a model

2. Implicit solver options

The implicit run uses the model's ROUTING_STEP as a fixed step and halves it only when Newton fails. Stock keeps its own variable step. θ below 1 is less damped and failed on two of the sixteen test models.

Nothing run yet.

What was measured before this shipped

    
    
      
  • Off means stock. With the extension switched off the engine's .out file is byte-identical to pristine EPA SWMM 5.2.4 on all 16 test models.
    • 
      
  • One engine, one answer. This wasm engine is byte-identical to a native musl build of the same source on all 16 models, extension off and on. A glibc build, checked on four of the models, differs from it by at most 7e-7 ft and 3e-8 cfs.
    • 
      
  • Against stock dynamic wave on the 16 models: conduit peak flows within 5.5%, node peak depths within 9.8%, routing continuity within 0.11%, no step accepted unconverged.
    • 
      
  • Cost. At the same 5 s step the implicit run took 16 times as long as stock on the chain model (range 15.0 to 16.4 over seven interleaved pairs), and 8.7 times on the pump model.
    • 
    

    
What this does not show

    
    
      
  • No comparison with InfoWorks ICM itself, and no field data. Agreement with stock SWMM says the two schemes solve the same equations, not that either is right.
    • 
      
  • The test models have 3 to 8 conduits. Nothing the size of a real network has been run.
    • 
      
  • Not modelled: conduit flap gates, culvert inlet control, force-main equations (Manning is used), conduit seepage and evaporation, conduit flow limits. The report counts any it meets.
    • 
      
  • Every conduit keeps a base depth of 5% of its height, so reported link depths never fall below that. Link flows and volumes are net of the base flow.
    • 
    

    
AI use

    
This bench and the solver in it were built with Claude, Anthropic's AI model, in a claude.ai session in October 2026, under the direction of Robert (Bob) Dickinson. He asked for the solver, chose to put it in SWMM 5.2.4 and is running the InfoWorks ICM comparison himself; responsibility for the work is his. Claude wrote pbox.c and its hooks into the engine, compiled the WebAssembly engine, wrote the sixteen test models, this page and its text, and found and fixed the convergence faults. The checks above are mechanical (byte comparisons and engine runs), not a human code review. No comparison with InfoWorks ICM has been made yet.

    
License: pbox.c and this page are public domain, like EPA SWMM 5. The bundled WASI shim (@bjorn3/browser_wasi_shim) is MIT or Apache-2.0; the engine statically links wasi-libc and LLVM compiler-rt. How to use this bench

  
    
    
  1. Pick a model. Sixteen small test networks are built in, or load your own .inp. It must use FLOW_ROUTING DYNWAVE.
    2. 
    
  2. Leave the options at their defaults for a first run.
    3. 
    
  3. Run both engines. The same file goes through stock dynamic wave and then the implicit box scheme.
    4. 
    
  4. Read the summary. Continuity, outflow, flooding and how hard the implicit solver had to work.
    5. 
    
  5. Compare an element. Overlay any link flow or node depth, then check the table of largest peak changes.
    6. 
    
  6. Try a 60 s ROUTING_STEP. The two "60 s step" samples show the implicit scheme holding a step stock cannot use at its Courant limit.
    7.
